strategies.title: [bounded-vnd-local] Conflict-aware variable-neighborhood descent
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: bounded-vnd-local  
Replacement scope: Replace the incumbent’s final adjacent-interchange-only improvement loop with a bounded variable-neighborhood descent over relocations, bounded-distance swaps, and short segment reversals, retaining the existing beam and greedy construction unchanged.  
Compute budget: At most 4 descent rounds; per round, test relocations up to distance 12 in either direction, swaps at distances 2 through 6, and reversals of lengths 3 through 8; stop immediately at the existing per-workload deadline, with a modest additional simulator-call cost after construction.  
Gain mechanism: The incumbent can only accept a sequence of individually improving adjacent swaps, so it cannot cross an adjacent-swap local minimum when moving one transaction several positions is beneficial only as a whole; relocation and short reversal moves directly alter the ordering of a conflict cluster while maintaining a complete permutation. The implementation starts from the incumbent’s best complete schedule, evaluates every trial through `get_opt_seq_cost`, accepts only strict improvements, and preserves the current valid schedule as fallback.  
Observed bottleneck: the measured best parent already obtains makespan 264, while the prior broad insertion/swap implementation scored 503 because it weakened construction and over-spent its budget; therefore the safer opportunity is a bounded local replacement after the successful beam constructor.  
Expected-gain check: this is falsifiable if the three-workload total makespan is at most 263, because `1000000 / (1 + 263) = 3787.878...`, strictly exceeding the current combined score 3773.5849, and the incumbent cannot realize a strictly beneficial non-monotone relocation trapped behind non-improving adjacent exchanges.

strategies.title: [destroy-repair-lns] Contiguous conflict-cluster destroy-and-cheapest-repair
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: destroy-repair-lns  
Replacement scope: Replace the randomized greedy-restart phase with a bounded large-neighborhood search seeded by the best beam completion; keep beam construction and final local descent.  
Compute budget: Use at most `max(4, num_seqs)` destroy-repair attempts, each removing one contiguous block of 3 to 8 transactions from the incumbent or an accepted improved schedule; repair one removed transaction at a time by testing every insertion position, with at most two repair orders per destroyed block and a hard deadline check in every inner loop.  
Gain mechanism: A contiguous block in an order often contains transactions coupled by delayed read/write conflicts; removing it permits the repair procedure to place its members on both sides of transactions that the original greedy prefix committed too early. This changes a mesoscopic portion of the schedule rather than requiring every intermediate adjacent swap to improve. For each repair order, start from the surviving permutation, insert every removed transaction at its minimum true full-schedule-cost position, and retain the resulting complete permutation only if its recomputed full cost is lower.  
Observed bottleneck: beam-prefix ranking uses costs of incomplete schedules, so it can prune a prefix whose transactions must later be separated by a group of conflict-mediating transactions; a block destroy-and-repair explicitly reoptimizes that omitted ordering decision.  
Expected-gain check: this is falsifiable if any repaired schedule reduces the total true makespan from 264 to 263 or below, which is sufficient for combined score above 3773.5849, and the incumbent’s one-transaction-at-a-time greedy completion cannot perform the same simultaneous removal and reinsertion of an already committed block.

strategies.title: [global-cheapest-insertion] Full-order cheapest-insertion constructor
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: global-cheapest-insertion  
Replacement scope: Replace both the partial-prefix beam construction and randomized greedy-restart construction with a deterministic multistart cheapest-insertion constructor, followed by the existing bounded local refinement.  
Compute budget: Use at most `min(max(3, num_seqs), 10)` starts: identity, reverse identity, and remaining starts selected by deterministic cyclic transaction IDs; on each construction step score at most 12 candidate unplaced transactions, and for each selected transaction score every insertion position in the current complete partial order; perform no more than one insertion pass per start and obey the same 105-second per-workload deadline.  
Gain mechanism: Rather than irrevocably appending transactions to a prefix, this construction can insert a newly selected transaction into the middle of the current sequence, immediately separating two conflicting transactions that a prefix-only beam must keep contiguous. At each step, choose the candidate transaction/insertion position with minimum simulator cost over the partial sequence; rotate the candidate window across starts so every transaction is considered early in at least one construction. The resulting sequence is always a unique ordering of all inserted IDs, then is completed with uninserted IDs if time expires, preserving validity.  
Observed bottleneck: the current construction has only append edges in its search topology—once a transaction is selected early, it can never move behind a later transaction except through the weak final adjacent descent—whereas insertion construction has direct middle-placement edges.  
Expected-gain check: this is falsifiable if the evaluator reports total makespan 263 or lower, and the new degree of freedom is a direct insertion between previously selected transactions, a move unavailable to the incumbent’s beam-prefix construction before local search.

strategies.title: [beam-prefix-construction] Diverse true-cost beam construction
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: beam-prefix-construction  
Replacement scope: Replace the bounded cyclic-window cheapest-insertion construction phase with a deterministic beam search over partial transaction permutations; retain only a compact global relocation refinement afterward.  
Compute budget: One construction run per workload, beam width 8–10, at most `beam_width * n * (n + 1) / 2` partial-schedule simulator evaluations (about 50,000 for 100 transactions), followed by at most two full best-improvement relocation passes; enforce a 112-second per-workload deadline.  
Gain mechanism: The incumbent commits to one partial order at every insertion depth and only varies the next transaction within a small rotated window. A beam retains several incompatible prefix orderings simultaneously, allowing later conflict-heavy transactions to be arranged behind different predecessor sets before committing to a complete permutation. At each depth, extend every retained prefix by every remaining transaction, rank the resulting partial schedules by true simulator makespan, and retain the best unique prefixes. Complete any interrupted prefixes with remaining IDs in deterministic order, evaluate complete schedules, and retain the best valid permutation. Every emitted candidate contains each transaction at most once; final completion appends every missing ID exactly once. The observed bottleneck is premature construction commitment rather than lack of small local moves. Expected-gain check: this construction explores prefix-contact topologies that the single-path insertion constructor cannot realize, and it is falsifiably successful if the evaluator finds total makespan at most 238, which yields `1000000 / 239 = 4184.10`, strictly above 4166.67.

strategies.title: [global-relocate-descent] Exact whole-permutation relocate neighborhood
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: global-relocate-descent  
Replacement scope: Replace the bounded-distance first-improvement relocation, non-adjacent swap, and short-reversal refinement block with global best-improvement relocation descent.  
Compute budget: Start from the incumbent constructor’s best complete permutation; perform at most three passes, each evaluating every remove-and-reinsert position (`n * (n - 1)` candidates, approximately 9,900 at 100 transactions), stopping at the per-workload deadline.  
Gain mechanism: The current relocation scan limits motion to a short distance and accepts the first improvement found, so a transaction cannot directly cross a distant conflict cluster and an early small improvement can conceal a much better move. For each pass, remove each transaction once, test reinsertion in every possible position, select the single lowest true-cost complete permutation over the whole relocate neighborhood, and repeat only if that global move strictly improves makespan. This is a local exploitation mechanism with a new global movement topology, not a tuning change to the current bounded scan. Removal followed by insertion preserves a complete transaction-ID permutation exactly. The observed bottleneck is that current refinement cannot test long-range precedence changes. Expected-gain check: the new neighborhood includes every incumbent bounded relocation but additionally allows a transaction to cross any number of conflicting transactions, and it is falsifiably successful if total makespan is at most 238, corresponding to combined score 4184.10.

strategies.title: [dispersed-regret-repair] Noncontiguous ruin with regret-based repair
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: dispersed-regret-repair  
Replacement scope: Replace the final VND phase with an iterated noncontiguous destroy-and-regret-repair phase operating on the best complete permutation from construction.  
Compute budget: At most six repair rounds per workload; each round removes 10–16 transactions selected at evenly spaced schedule positions with a round-dependent coprime stride, and reconstructs them using at most 16 insertion positions per removed transaction; finish with one global relocation pass if time remains.  
Gain mechanism: Contiguous block modifications preserve most existing predecessor/successor contacts and therefore cannot jointly relocate several transactions whose conflicts are distributed across the schedule. In each round, remove a dispersed set of transaction IDs, leaving a valid backbone. During repair, evaluate every removed transaction’s best and second-best insertion costs into the current backbone; insert the transaction with largest regret first at its best position, then repeat. Regret prioritizes transactions whose placement is constrained by the already fixed conflict contacts, while the dispersed destruction permits several distant precedence relations to change together. Keep only strictly better full schedules and always preserve the original best schedule as fallback. Removing IDs and reinserting each exactly once preserves validity. The observed bottleneck is mesoscopic conflict structure spanning nonadjacent schedule regions. Expected-gain check: the repair can change multiple separated transaction contacts in one accepted move, which neither a single relocate nor a contiguous reversal can realize, and it is falsifiably successful if evaluator total makespan is at most 238 and combined score therefore exceeds 4166.67.

strategies.title: [critical-window-exact] Exact contiguous-window permutation descent
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: critical-window-exact  
Replacement scope: Replace the existing bounded VND relocation/swap/reversal phase after construction.  
Compute budget: At most 2 passes; at most 12 windows per pass; each window has size 5 and therefore at most 120 true-cost evaluations, for at most 2,880 uncached neighborhood evaluations per workload, stopping at a 116-second per-workload deadline.  
Gain mechanism: The incumbent only accepts single relocations, swaps, and reversals, which can require passing through a worse intermediate permutation before a coordinated five-transaction order becomes beneficial. For each selected contiguous window, hold all outside transaction positions fixed and enumerate every ordering of the window under the true simulator objective. This changes the relative precedence topology of up to five transactions simultaneously, including patterns unreachable by one accepted VND move. Start from the incumbent schedule, retain only strict improvements, and keep the original schedule as fallback; every candidate is created by replacing a same-size slice, so it remains a complete permutation of transaction IDs.  
Observed bottleneck: the incumbent’s local phase is restricted to narrow first-improving move classes and can stop at a local minimum despite remaining clustered conflict orderings. The falsifiable expected-gain check is that this mechanism should be retained only if the evaluator finds total true makespan at most 238, which yields `1000000 / 239 = 4184.1004`, strictly above the current 4166.6667 ranking score.

strategies.title: [block-cross-exchange] Separated block exchange with exact internal orientations
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: block-cross-exchange  
Replacement scope: Replace the current non-adjacent swap and short-reversal portions of VND with a mesoscopic separated-block exchange phase.  
Compute budget: Scan at most 24 deterministic pairs of non-overlapping blocks per descent pass, with block lengths 3 or 4; test the direct exchange plus the four orientation combinations (forward/reversed for each block), for at most 120 true-cost evaluations per pass and at most 4 passes per workload. Expected evaluation-time effect is small relative to the current insertion phase.  
Gain mechanism: A single non-adjacent swap moves only two transactions and a short reversal changes only local orientation. Instead, select two separated contiguous regions, exchange their positions as units, and independently choose forward or reversed orientation for each moved region. This can move a conflict-heavy group ahead of another group while preserving useful local ordering within either group, a contact-topology change not represented by the incumbent’s individual relocation or pairwise swap neighborhoods. Select block-pair locations deterministically from evenly spaced starts plus offsets based on the current pass, evaluate every prescribed orientation with `workload.get_opt_seq_cost`, and accept the best strict improvement before restarting the scan. Because exchanged slices have equal retained membership and all untouched entries remain in place, each candidate is a valid complete permutation.  
Observed bottleneck: the schedule may contain correctly ordered local clusters in the wrong global relative order, for which transaction-by-transaction moves create harmful intermediate schedules. The falsifiable expected-gain check is that a successful exchange must reduce the recomputed three-workload total below 239; otherwise it supplies no score improvement over the current measured makespan.

strategies.title: [full-cheapest-insertion] Complete-pool true-cost insertion construction
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: full-cheapest-insertion  
Replacement scope: Replace the bounded rotating 12-transaction candidate window in the construction phase with globally cheapest insertion over every currently unplaced transaction and every insertion position.  
Compute budget: At most 2 deterministic starts per workload, seeded by transaction 0 and transaction `n - 1`; each start performs no more than `sum_{k=1}^{n-1} k(n-k)` candidate evaluations, approximately `n^3 / 6` per start, under a hard 116-second deadline. Use remaining time only for a bounded exact-window phase.  
Gain mechanism: The incumbent can permanently exclude the transaction that should be inserted next because only 12 rotating remaining transactions are considered at each depth. Full-pool insertion removes this active-set restriction: at every partial order, it evaluates the actual simulator cost of every legal next transaction-position pair and chooses the global minimum. Different seeds provide distinct early precedence commitments while retaining deterministic reproducibility. A valid identity permutation is evaluated before search, interrupted constructions are completed by appending all remaining IDs, and all generated orders are permutations by construction.  
Observed bottleneck: the current construction’s bounded candidate window, rather than its final cost comparison, can lock the search into an inferior global arrangement before local search begins. The falsifiable expected-gain check is that the complete-pool construction introduces legal next-insertion choices the incumbent cannot inspect at the same depth and succeeds only if evaluator recomputation reports total makespan at most 238, equivalent to combined score at least 4184.1004.

strategies.title: [tabu-permutation-walk] Aspiration tabu search over complete schedules
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: tabu-permutation-walk  
Replacement scope: Replace the bounded VND refinement block after the current cheapest-insertion constructor.  
Compute budget: 6 tabu-search starts seeded by the best completed insertion schedules; each start is limited to 80 accepted moves and at most 36 true-cost move evaluations per move, with a strict per-workload deadline of 112 seconds. This reduces repeated exhaustive nearby scans and reserves explicit time for escape moves.  
Gain mechanism: The observed bottleneck is that first-improving relocation/swap/reversal descent can only accept improving schedules, so it becomes trapped when reducing one current conflict delay temporarily increases another. Use a tabu tenure of 7 accepted moves on inverse relocations and swapped transaction pairs, select the lowest-cost non-tabu sampled move even if it worsens the current schedule, and retain a separate global best under the true simulator cost. Include aspiration when a tabu move beats the global best. The move neighborhood consists of deterministic dispersed relocations and swaps, so every candidate remains a complete permutation; retain the original complete insertion result as fallback. This explores conflict-order rearrangements inaccessible to strict descent. Expected-gain check: this is falsified unless the evaluator finds a total makespan below 239, because the incumbent cannot traverse a strictly worsening intermediate permutation while retaining its best schedule.

strategies.title: [conflict-signature-seriation] Graph-derived transaction ordering followed by tr
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: conflict-signature-seriation  
Replacement scope: Replace the multistart seed-order and partial candidate-window selection in the construction phase, while leaving one short true-cost refinement pass afterward.  
Compute budget: 4 deterministic constructions, each with at most one complete transaction-pair conflict-matrix build and at most `min(10, remaining)` insertion candidates at every construction depth; one 40-move local refinement pass per completed construction. Expected cost-evaluation volume is lower than the present serial 10-start construction because structural ordering is computed without simulator calls.  
Gain mechanism: Parse each transaction’s operation string, build a symmetric weighted conflict graph where a pair receives one unit for every shared key for which at least one operation is a write, and construct four graph seriations: descending weighted degree, reverse degree, greedy maximum-affinity path, and reverse affinity path. In the affinity path, repeatedly append the unplaced transaction with maximum total conflict weight to the last two placed transactions, breaking ties by transaction ID. Feed each resulting order into a position-by-position true-cost insertion constructor, considering the next unplaced transactions in that seriation rather than a rotating ID window. This changes the construction topology from arbitrary ID windows to deliberately adjacent high-contention transactions, exposing globally coherent conflict arrangements before the simulator-based decisions begin. Parsing failures simply use zero weights and retain valid ID-order fallback; all final schedules are explicitly checked as permutations. Expected-gain check: this is falsified unless at least one seriation-derived construction or its refinement yields total makespan below 239; the incumbent’s rotating candidate window has no degree of freedom for globally grouping transactions by actual read/write conflict contact.

strategies.title: [exact-partition-ordering] Dynamic-programmed ordering of conflict-connected tra
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: exact-partition-ordering  
Replacement scope: Replace the entire initial permutation construction with a mesoscopic module construction; retain a bounded true-cost relocation cleanup only after modules have been assembled.  
Compute budget: Build the conflict graph once; form deterministic modules by greedy maximum-affinity agglomeration until every module has at most 6 transactions; enumerate all internal module permutations (at most 720 per module) only when the module is first formed; use Held-Karp subset dynamic programming for the order of at most 12 modules, otherwise greedily merge the lowest-affinity modules until there are 12. Cap simulator evaluations at 30,000 per workload and stop at 108 seconds.  
Gain mechanism: The current constructor commits individual transactions one at a time, which cannot jointly choose the internal arrangement of a conflict-dense group and its placement relative to another group. Form conflict-connected modules from the operation-derived write/read conflict graph, enumerate each small module’s internal orientations, and score a module orientation by inserting the entire oriented block into a growing schedule using the true simulator cost. At the outer level, dynamic programming uses graph cut weight as the transition surrogate to enumerate module orders, then evaluates the best few resulting complete schedules with the true simulator and applies bounded cleanup. The invariant is that every candidate is a concatenation of disjoint transaction modules and therefore a complete permutation; if the cap interrupts enumeration, concatenate all remaining modules in deterministic ID order. Expected-gain check: this is falsified unless one jointly oriented module schedule has total makespan below 239; the incumbent has no move that selects an entire internally permuted conflict module as one construction decision.

strategies.title: ordered attempt [tabu-permutation-walk] Aspiration tabu search over complete schedules
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: tabu-permutation-walk  
Replacement scope: Replace the bounded VND refinement block after the current cheapest-insertion constructor.  
Compute budget: 6 tabu-search starts seeded by the best completed insertion schedules; each start is limited to 80 accepted moves and at most 36 true-cost move evaluations per move, with a strict per-workload deadline of 112 seconds. This reduces repeated exhaustive nearby scans and reserves explicit time for escape moves.  
Gain mechanism: The observed bottleneck is that first-improving relocation/swap/reversal descent can only accept improving schedules, so it becomes trapped when reducing one current conflict delay temporarily increases another. Use a tabu tenure of 7 accepted moves on inverse relocations and swapped transaction pairs, select the lowest-cost non-tabu sampled move even if it worsens the current schedule, and retain a separate global best under the true simulator cost. Include aspiration when a tabu move beats the global best. The move neighborhood consists of deterministic dispersed relocations and swaps, so every candidate remains a complete permutation; retain the original complete insertion result as fallback. This explores conflict-order rearrangements inaccessible to strict descent. Expected-gain check: this is falsified unless the evaluator finds a total makespan below 239, because the incumbent cannot traverse a strictly worsening intermediate permutation while retaining its best schedule.

strategies.title: ordered attempt [conflict-signature-seriation] Graph-derived transaction ordering followed by tr
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: conflict-signature-seriation  
Replacement scope: Replace the multistart seed-order and partial candidate-window selection in the construction phase, while leaving one short true-cost refinement pass afterward.  
Compute budget: 4 deterministic constructions, each with at most one complete transaction-pair conflict-matrix build and at most `min(10, remaining)` insertion candidates at every construction depth; one 40-move local refinement pass per completed construction. Expected cost-evaluation volume is lower than the present serial 10-start construction because structural ordering is computed without simulator calls.  
Gain mechanism: Parse each transaction’s operation string, build a symmetric weighted conflict graph where a pair receives one unit for every shared key for which at least one operation is a write, and construct four graph seriations: descending weighted degree, reverse degree, greedy maximum-affinity path, and reverse affinity path. In the affinity path, repeatedly append the unplaced transaction with maximum total conflict weight to the last two placed transactions, breaking ties by transaction ID. Feed each resulting order into a position-by-position true-cost insertion constructor, considering the next unplaced transactions in that seriation rather than a rotating ID window. This changes the construction topology from arbitrary ID windows to deliberately adjacent high-contention transactions, exposing globally coherent conflict arrangements before the simulator-based decisions begin. Parsing failures simply use zero weights and retain valid ID-order fallback; all final schedules are explicitly checked as permutations. Expected-gain check: this is falsified unless at least one seriation-derived construction or its refinement yields total makespan below 239; the incumbent’s rotating candidate window has no degree of freedom for globally grouping transactions by actual read/write conflict contact.

strategies.title: ordered attempt [exact-partition-ordering] Dynamic-programmed ordering of conflict-connected tra
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: exact-partition-ordering  
Replacement scope: Replace the entire initial permutation construction with a mesoscopic module construction; retain a bounded true-cost relocation cleanup only after modules have been assembled.  
Compute budget: Build the conflict graph once; form deterministic modules by greedy maximum-affinity agglomeration until every module has at most 6 transactions; enumerate all internal module permutations (at most 720 per module) only when the module is first formed; use Held-Karp subset dynamic programming for the order of at most 12 modules, otherwise greedily merge the lowest-affinity modules until there are 12. Cap simulator evaluations at 30,000 per workload and stop at 108 seconds.  
Gain mechanism: The current constructor commits individual transactions one at a time, which cannot jointly choose the internal arrangement of a conflict-dense group and its placement relative to another group. Form conflict-connected modules from the operation-derived write/read conflict graph, enumerate each small module’s internal orientations, and score a module orientation by inserting the entire oriented block into a growing schedule using the true simulator cost. At the outer level, dynamic programming uses graph cut weight as the transition surrogate to enumerate module orders, then evaluates the best few resulting complete schedules with the true simulator and applies bounded cleanup. The invariant is that every candidate is a concatenation of disjoint transaction modules and therefore a complete permutation; if the cap interrupts enumeration, concatenate all remaining modules in deterministic ID order. Expected-gain check: this is falsified unless one jointly oriented module schedule has total makespan below 239; the incumbent has no move that selects an entire internally permuted conflict module as one construction decision.

strategies.title: [ejection-chain-neighborhood] Conflict-aware cyclic ejection-chain descent
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: ejection-chain-neighborhood

Replacement scope: Replace the current bounded VND refinement block after the cheapest-insertion construction; retain the constructor and its best complete permutation fallback unchanged.

Compute budget: At most 3 accepted ejection-chain rounds per workload; enumerate at most 8 anchor positions, 10 first relocation destinations per anchor, and 8 second-item reinsertion destinations per attempted chain. Stop at the existing per-workload deadline. This adds at most 1,920 true-cost evaluations per round and should fit by reserving the final 12 seconds of each workload budget for refinement.

Gain mechanism: The observed refinement variants can worsen the result because a single relocate, swap, or reversal often crosses an intermediate schedule with higher makespan even when the final combined rearrangement is beneficial. An ejection chain removes transaction A, inserts it elsewhere, ejects the displaced transaction B from that region, and reinserts B into a third position before evaluating the complete resulting permutation once. This creates a coordinated three-contact rearrangement that neither a single relocation nor a pairwise swap can represent as one accepted move. Each candidate is formed by removing and reinserting existing IDs only, so it remains a complete permutation; retain the prior best schedule unless its true simulator cost strictly improves. Expected-gain check: this is falsified unless the evaluator reaches total makespan at most 238, which would yield \(1{,}000{,}000/(1+238)=4184.10\), strictly above 4166.67, through a three-position transformation unavailable to the incumbent’s accepted one-move descent.

strategies.title: [elite-path-relinking] Mesoscopic order path relinking among insertion elites
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: elite-path-relinking

Replacement scope: Replace the “keep only the current best constructed sequence” behavior in the multistart construction phase with an elite archive of the best 4 completed cheapest-insertion schedules, then replace final VND with deterministic path relinking between archive pairs.

Compute budget: Keep the existing maximum 10 construction starts, but reserve 18 seconds before the per-workload deadline for relinking. Archive at most 4 complete schedules. For each of at most 6 archive pairs, run at most 2 directed relinking paths, each with at most `n` evaluated intermediate schedules; at each step move the earliest transaction whose position differs from the target into its target position. Stop immediately on deadline.

Gain mechanism: Different insertion seeds can encode different good transaction-contact topologies, but the incumbent discards all non-best topologies and only makes small local changes to the surviving schedule. Directed relinking walks through valid permutations between two independently good full orders and evaluates the intermediate contact arrangements. These intermediate schedules can combine a useful prefix/cluster ordering from one insertion solution with the later conflict resolution of another without relying on random destruction or on a local move being independently improving. Every state is generated by a remove-and-insert operation over a full permutation and is therefore valid; preserve the original best archive member as fallback. Expected-gain check: the hypothesis is falsified unless at least one evaluated intermediate has total makespan at most 238, the threshold corresponding to combined score 4184.10, because the incumbent never evaluates a trajectory joining two completed insertion topologies.

strategies.title: [permutation-genetic-recombination] Structural precedence-preserving permutation
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: permutation-genetic-recombination

Replacement scope: Replace the cyclic-window cheapest-insertion constructor with a bounded population constructor: produce 8 deterministic seed orders using alternating forward/reverse transaction-ID sweeps and conflict-sensitive greedy insertion, then evolve them with order crossover and survivor selection. Do not append the old multistart constructor as a second pipeline.

Compute budget: Population size 8, at most 8 generations, exactly 8 offspring per generation, and at most 2 mutation attempts per offspring. Use order crossover: copy a contiguous parent-A segment and fill remaining positions in parent-B order; optionally apply one relocate mutation. Evaluate every offspring with the true simulator cost and keep the best 8 unique permutations. Limit total offspring evaluations to 64 per workload, leaving the existing final local-search budget unchanged. Runtime is materially lower than repeated all-position insertion scans.

Gain mechanism: Cheapest insertion commits every early placement and can only vary seeds and the currently visible candidate window. Order crossover introduces a structural degree of freedom absent from that construction: it transfers a whole internally compatible transaction subsequence from one schedule while retaining the relative ordering of all remaining transactions from another. This permits conflict clusters discovered in separate seed constructions to coexist in a single schedule, rather than requiring one greedy construction to discover all favorable contacts in one path. Order crossover contains each ID exactly once by construction, and relocate mutation likewise preserves a full permutation. Expected-gain check: accept the structural hypothesis only if the evolved population produces total makespan at most 238, yielding combined score 4184.10; this threshold tests whether preserving a parent segment while importing the other parent’s complement realizes a topology no one greedy insertion history can directly construct.

strategies.title: [segment-relocation-descent] Contiguous transaction-block relocation
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: segment-relocation-descent

Replacement scope: Replace the current final bounded VND phase, specifically the individual relocation / non-adjacent swap / reversal loops, with first-improving contiguous-block relocation followed by a short adjacent-swap cleanup.

Compute budget: At most 3 descent rounds; for each round test blocks of lengths 2 through 5, every source location, and every reinsertion location, stopping on the first strict true-cost improvement. Reserve 20–25 seconds of each 119-second per-workload budget for this phase by ending construction early. Expected evaluation-time effect: bounded O(4n²) true-cost calls per descent round, with deadline checks before every block and target scan.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent can move one transaction, swap two transactions, or reverse a small interval, but cannot preserve the internally useful order of a conflict-coupled group while moving that entire group across another group. Block relocation introduces this missing contact topology: for example, a sequence of transactions sharing several read/write keys can remain mutually well arranged while being moved before or after the transactions that delay its critical conflict path. Start from the incumbent’s valid cheapest-insertion result, remove `seq[i:i+length]`, and insert it at every position of the remaining order; every candidate is automatically a complete permutation. Accept only strict simulator-cost improvements and retain the incumbent as fallback. The observed bottleneck is that existing refinements use only single-item or exchange-like moves after a constructor that can lock correlated transactions into the wrong macro-position; this move changes macro-position without destroying the correlated local ordering. Expected-gain check: this is falsified unless the evaluator reaches total makespan at most 238, which would produce `1000000 / 239 = 4184.1004`, strictly above 4166.6667; the incumbent cannot realize a nontrivial intact length-2-to-5 relocation in one local move.

strategies.title: [precedence-tournament-construction] Pairwise simulator-derived precedence order
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: precedence-tournament-construction

Replacement scope: Replace the cyclic bounded-window cheapest-insertion construction phase with a pairwise precedence-tournament constructor; retain a short true-cost insertion polish and the incumbent fallback.

Compute budget: Evaluate both orders for every unordered transaction pair, for at most `n(n-1)` partial-sequence simulator calls, then build at most 4 deterministic tournament orders and apply at most one complete cheapest-insertion pass per order. Stop construction at 90 seconds per workload and reserve the remaining time for one bounded local polish. Expected evaluation-time effect: predictable quadratic pair evaluation rather than repeated multistart partial-order evaluation.

Gain mechanism: For each pair `(a,b)`, compute the true simulator costs of `[a,b]` and `[b,a]`; orient the pair toward the lower-cost order and assign edge weight equal to the cost difference. Construct a weighted precedence order by repeatedly selecting the remaining transaction with the best weighted net preference against the remaining set, once forward and once backward; additionally construct two deterministic orders from weighted out-score and weighted in-score. Evaluate each full order, then run one true-cost cheapest insertion pass that can repair tournament cycles. This changes the construction representation from “which transaction looks cheap to insert into a current prefix” to an explicit all-pairs conflict-precedence topology. Every generated order contains each ID exactly once, and only complete permutations are passed to the final evaluator. The observed bottleneck is that the current constructor sees only a rotating window of at most 12 unplaced transactions at each depth, so a strongly conflicting pair can be missed until their relative order is effectively frozen. Expected-gain check: the hypothesis is falsified unless one tournament-derived complete order or its insertion polish attains total makespan at most 238, the threshold corresponding to combined score 4184.1004; the incumbent’s bounded candidate windows do not evaluate all pairwise precedence alternatives.

strategies.title: [position-distribution-search] Elite position-model permutation sampling
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: position-distribution-search

Replacement scope: Replace the multistart seed-order generation and construction restart policy with a bounded model-based permutation search; retain the simulator cost cache and a final deterministic local improvement phase.

Compute budget: Generate 12 initial complete permutations from deterministic cyclic, reverse-cyclic, and pairwise-score seeds; run at most 10 model-update generations with population 8, preserving the best 4 elite schedules each generation. Each sampled order is evaluated once by the true simulator. Cap the entire model search at 85 seconds per workload, leaving at least 25 seconds for block relocation or single-item descent. Expected evaluation-time effect: at most 92 complete-order evaluations plus bounded repair calls, substantially fewer than repeated global insertion evaluations.

Gain mechanism: Maintain a position-by-transaction frequency matrix from the elite schedules. For each sample, draw a permutation left-to-right without replacement, choosing among remaining transactions according to the smoothed elite frequency for the current position, with a deterministic low-discrepancy tie rotation rather than relying on uncontrolled random seeds. Add one sampled “anti-consensus” schedule per generation by selecting low-frequency feasible choices, allowing escape from an early shared ordering mistake. The representation is a distribution over complete schedules rather than a single prefix; it can simultaneously alter many transaction positions and discover coordinated orderings that no sequence of accepted one-move refinements reaches. Validity is preserved because sampling removes each selected transaction from the remaining-ID set and appends all remaining IDs if the deadline interrupts sampling. The observed bottleneck is the incumbent’s greedy construction commits one transaction and position at a time, making later choices conditional on a single early prefix; position-distribution search explores competing global arrangements while retaining objective-tested elites. Expected-gain check: the hypothesis is falsified unless its best sampled or polished schedule reduces the summed makespan to at most 238, yielding combined score 4184.1004; unlike the incumbent, one model sample can jointly move an arbitrary number of transactions to different global positions.

strategies.title: [adaptive-dispersed-destroy-repair] Simulator-scored dispersed ruin-and-repair
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: adaptive-dispersed-destroy-repair

Replacement scope: Replace the incumbent’s final contiguous block-relocation descent and adjacent-swap cleanup with a bounded destroy-and-cheapest-repair phase operating on the best complete permutation produced by the existing constructor.

Compute budget: At most 12 repair starts per workload; each removes at most 6 transactions and greedily reinserts each removed transaction by evaluating every legal insertion position. This is at most roughly 12 × 6 × n simulator evaluations, plus cached repeats, and fits inside the incumbent’s existing 22-second refinement reservation rather than extending the 119-second per-workload deadline.

Gain mechanism: The current refinement can move a contiguous block but cannot jointly relocate transactions that are separated by unrelated transactions. Remove a deterministic dispersed set of positions, retain the relative order of the complement, and greedily reinsert the removed transactions in alternating forward and reverse repair orders. This creates coordinated long-distance changes in several transaction contacts at once, including changes that no single contiguous relocation can produce. Every repair candidate remains a permutation because removal is by unique transaction IDs and each removed ID is inserted exactly once. The best full simulator-scored permutation remains the fallback.

Observed bottleneck: the incumbent’s best construction is followed by topology-preserving contiguous moves, which cannot repair conflict-coupled transactions distributed across the schedule.

Expected-gain check: this is falsifiable if the evaluator returns a total makespan below the incumbent’s 237; the new degree of freedom is a simultaneous noncontiguous removal/reinsertion pattern that contiguous block relocation cannot realize in one descent move.

strategies.title: [boundary-window-permutation] Exact small-window ordering around schedule bounda
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: boundary-window-permutation

Replacement scope: Replace only the adjacent-swap cleanup phase after construction and block descent with exact enumeration of permutations inside selected short schedule windows.

Compute budget: Enumerate all 4! orderings for at most 20 deterministic windows of length four, selected at evenly spaced schedule boundaries and around endpoints of any accepted block move; repeat for at most two passes. This is at most 960 full-cost calls per pass before cache hits, with no additional construction starts and a substantially smaller cost than the removed adjacent-swap scan.

Gain mechanism: Adjacent swaps change only one neighboring contact and can be trapped when improving a local four-transaction order requires a temporary worsening swap. For each chosen length-four window, keep all outside transactions fixed and evaluate every internal ordering under the true simulator objective. This exactly optimizes all local serial orders in that window and can cross a local barrier involving multiple conflicting read/write transaction pairs. Validity is preserved because each candidate replaces a window by a permutation of precisely the same IDs.

Observed bottleneck: the present cleanup accepts only immediately improving adjacent transpositions, so it cannot perform a three-cycle or reversal when the first adjacent swap is neutral or harmful.

Expected-gain check: this is falsifiable if any enumerated window yields a full simulator cost below 237 total makespan across the three workloads; its distinct capability is evaluating cyclic four-transaction reorderings unavailable to a first-improvement adjacent-swap descent.

strategies.title: [bidirectional-anchor-construction] Two-ended simulator-guided anchor growth
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: bidirectional-anchor-construction

Replacement scope: Replace the current seed-based globally cheapest-insertion construction phase, while retaining the incumbent’s cached true-cost evaluator and a final bounded local refinement phase.

Compute budget: Use at most 6 deterministic anchor pairs per workload. For each pair, initialize a left and right anchor transaction, then alternately choose among a bounded candidate set the transaction and side whose partial sequence has the lowest simulator cost; after the two chains are grown, merge by greedily inserting the right-chain transactions into the left chain in reverse construction order. Bound candidate consideration to 10 unplaced transactions per expansion and reserve at least 24 seconds for local refinement. The evaluation-time effect is comparable to the incumbent’s bounded insertion construction.

Gain mechanism: Current construction grows from one seed and immediately commits each selected transaction into a single evolving sequence. Two-ended anchor growth explicitly creates independent early and late transaction neighborhoods before connecting them, allowing high-conflict transactions to be deliberately placed at opposite temporal ends rather than competing for nearby insertion positions from one seed. Anchor pairs are deterministic combinations of low IDs, high IDs, and evenly spaced IDs, avoiding dependence on random seeds. Each completed schedule is a complete permutation because every transaction is assigned once to exactly one chain and merging only reorders assigned IDs.

Observed bottleneck: the incumbent’s single-seed partial order can make early insertion decisions dominate both schedule endpoints, reducing construction diversity despite multiple seeds.

Expected-gain check: this is falsifiable if the best bidirectional construction plus the retained refinement produces total makespan below 237; the mechanism’s new degree of freedom is independently choosing both endpoint neighborhoods before their merge, which the one-seed growth process does not represent.

Each completed schedule is a complete permutation because every transaction is assigned once to exactly one chain and merging only reorders assigned IDs.

strategies.title: ordered attempt [boundary-window-permutation] Exact small-window ordering around schedule bounda
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: boundary-window-permutation

Replacement scope: Replace only the adjacent-swap cleanup phase after construction and block descent with exact enumeration of permutations inside selected short schedule windows.

Compute budget: Enumerate all 4! orderings for at most 20 deterministic windows of length four, selected at evenly spaced schedule boundaries and around endpoints of any accepted block move; repeat for at most two passes. This is at most 960 full-cost calls per pass before cache hits, with no additional construction starts and a substantially smaller cost than the removed adjacent-swap scan.

Gain mechanism: Adjacent swaps change only one neighboring contact and can be trapped when improving a local four-transaction order requires a temporary worsening swap. For each chosen length-four window, keep all outside transactions fixed and evaluate every internal ordering under the true simulator objective. This exactly optimizes all local serial orders in that window and can cross a local barrier involving multiple conflicting read/write transaction pairs. Validity is preserved because each candidate replaces a window by a permutation of precisely the same IDs.

strategies.title: [segment-reversal-descent] critical-order inversion escape
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: segment-reversal-descent

Replacement scope: Replace the final adjacent-swap cleanup phase only; retain the existing cheapest-insertion construction and contiguous block-relocation descent.

Compute budget: At most two first-improvement passes; in each pass test reversals of contiguous segments of lengths 3 through 8, stopping immediately on the first strict improvement and always respecting the existing per-workload deadline. This adds at most \(2 \sum_{l=3}^{8}(n-l+1)\) simulator evaluations if time is available, with no material increase because it uses the time already reserved for refinement.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent can move a contiguous block while preserving its internal order, or swap only neighboring transactions. It cannot directly flip an internally misoriented conflict chain without traversing worse intermediate schedules. Reversing a segment changes many pairwise transaction precedences simultaneously, which can remove a cyclicly misplaced chain of write/read conflicts that block relocation preserves. Every candidate remains a complete permutation because reversal only rearranges an existing slice of `best_seq`; retain the incumbent schedule unless a true simulator cost is strictly lower.

Observed bottleneck: the current final cleanup has only an adjacent transposition neighborhood after macro relocation, so it is unable to cross local barriers requiring several precedence inversions at once. Expected-gain check: this is falsified unless the evaluator finds total makespan at most 236, which would yield \(1000000/(1+236)=4219.409\ldots\), strictly above 4201.680672.

strategies.title: [critical-skeleton-repair] deletion-criticality beam reinsertion
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: critical-skeleton-repair

Replacement scope: Replace one of the three contiguous block-relocation rounds with a mesoscopic repair round applied to the best completed schedule.

Compute budget: Score deletion of every transaction once, select the six transactions whose deletion produces the largest simulator-cost reduction, and remove them simultaneously. Reinsert them using a deterministic beam of width 6: for each beam state, evaluate every remaining removed transaction at every insertion position, retain the six lowest-cost complete partial skeletons, and stop at six insertions. Run at most one repair round per workload, only before the existing refinement deadline. This is bounded by roughly \(n + 6 \times 6 \times 6n\) evaluations in the worst case, and should replace rather than add a block-relocation round.

Gain mechanism: A contiguous relocation can only repair transactions already adjacent in the schedule. This repair uses deletion marginal cost to identify transactions participating in the current critical delay, then allows their relative order and their contacts with the fixed skeleton to change jointly. The beam preserves several incompatible partial arrangements instead of greedily committing to one insertion. The skeleton plus each ordered reinsertion is always a complete unique-ID permutation once all six are restored; if the deadline interrupts, return the retained incumbent or the best fully restored beam member.

Observed bottleneck: the current block descent tests one motion at a time and cannot jointly alter several separated high-impact transactions. Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is simultaneous reordering and reinsertion of six deletion-critical transactions across the entire fixed skeleton, which no incumbent block move or adjacent swap can realize in one accepted transition; it is successful only if the recomputed total makespan is below 237.

strategies.title: [agglomerative-order-merge] simulator-scored hierarchical schedule construction
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: agglomerative-order-merge

Replacement scope: Replace the bounded-window cheapest-insertion construction phase with a separate full-order construction, while retaining the incumbent initial identity schedule, cost cache, and final local refinement as fallback.

Compute budget: Build singleton ordered clusters. For each merge level, evaluate both concatenation directions for at most 24 deterministic cluster-pair candidates selected by cyclic scan of the current cluster list; merge the best pair and continue until one cluster remains. Run at most three different cyclic scans/starting offsets. This is at most \(3 \times 24 \times (n-1) \times 2\) partial simulator evaluations, substantially below the incumbent’s repeated transaction-by-position insertion evaluation count.

Gain mechanism: Cheapest insertion commits one transaction at a time into a largely fixed order. Hierarchical merging instead preserves internally beneficial transaction chains as ordered clusters and chooses which cluster contacts which other cluster next. Thus it explores a different contact topology: transactions that cooperate on conflicting keys can remain adjacent as a unit while the construction decides the macro ordering of whole chains. Each merge concatenates disjoint clusters, so the final cluster is provably a complete permutation of all transaction IDs; compare its true full cost against the existing complete incumbent before accepting it.

Observed bottleneck: the current construction’s width-12 insertion window can permanently miss a transaction whose useful placement depends on a later companion transaction. Expected-gain check: the construction can create a hierarchy of internally ordered conflict chains before choosing their inter-chain contacts, a structural state unavailable to singleton insertion after it commits those contacts; the falsifiable evaluator threshold is a total true makespan below 237.
